description: Report credential-shaped values in supplied configuration, by shape class and position, never by value. Recognises a PEM private key block, a JSON Web Token whose header actually decodes, documented key prefixes, a URL carrying a password, and a long run with the character mix of a generated key rather than of text. Also reports a field named like a credential whose value matches no listed shape. The shape classes are published in every response. Pay 180000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

allow_paths.description: Positions where a match is expected, such as an embedded image. A match there is noted as allowed rather than reported.

content.description: The configuration to scan, at most 262144 bytes. Nothing is fetched: no cloud account is contacted and no credential is accepted, so the document supplied is the whole input.

format.description: How to read the content. auto reads JSON when it parses as JSON and text otherwise, and says which it did. JSON positions are pointers; text positions are line numbers.

name: secret_shape_audit

clean.description: True only when no recognised shape was found. Not a statement that the content holds no secret: an unlisted format or an encoded value is not found.

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

matches.description: Per match: its position, shape class and length. Never its value.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

read_as.description: json or text, so a caller knows how positions are expressed.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

shape_classes.description: Every class looked for, published so a caller can see exactly what was and was not covered.

title: Secret Shape Audit
